items.title: New monthly price takes effect
items.quote: ab dem 01.06.2025 kostet Ihr Tarif „Netzwelt DSL 100“ 49,99 € statt bisher 44,99 € im Monat.
items.computation: The letter states the new price applies from a fixed calendar date, 01.06.2025. No counting needed, date is used as written.

items.title: Exercise special termination right (§ 57 Abs. 1 TKG) due to disadvantageous price change
items.quote: Das Kündigungsrecht besteht drei Monate ab Zugang dieser Mitteilung; der Vertrag endet frühestens zu dem Zeitpunkt, an dem der neue Preis wirksam wird.
items.computation: This is a private (non-authority) letter, so the statutory 3-/4-day deemed-delivery fiction for authorities does not apply; the period runs from actual Zugang (receipt), which is not stated in the letter. As no delivery date is given, I estimate receipt at 3 calendar days after the printed letter date (15.04.2025, a Tuesday) for ordinary domestic post, i.e. Zugang on Friday 18.04.2025. Per §187 Abs.1 BGB, the day of the triggering event (Zugang) is not counted; the 3-month period then ends on the day bearing the same number three months later: 18.04.2025 + 3 months = 18.07.2025. 18.07.2025 is a Friday, not a weekend or public holiday in NW, so no shift under §193 BGB is needed. Because the exact Zugang date is only an estimate (not stated in the letter), confidence is low.

warnings: The letter does not state the actual delivery/receipt (Zugang) date, only the print date of 15.04.2025; the 3-month special termination deadline was estimated assuming a 3-day postal transit time and should be verified against the customer's actual proof of receipt (e.g. postmark).

This is a private company notice, not an authority decision, so the statutory 3-/4-day deemed-delivery rule for authorities and the one-month Einspruch/Widerspruch framework do not apply; the only relevant deadline is the contractual 3-month special termination right under § 57 Abs. 1 TKG.
